distinguishing_scenario: First shell command without saved state changes a valid manifest: validation runs, no 'changed without a recognized command' note; the same change after a saved snapshot produces the note.
facet_text: On the initial manifest snapshot (no saved state for the active root) no change, removal or move notes are emitted; manifest and architecture validation still run and report findings.
rationale: post-tool-use.js:135 and 169-183 verified. FG-M1-3fc57e396d says unexplained manifest/project changes and every removal or move 'are reported'; it does not state the initial-snapshot exception, while FG-M1-cf5ed1aba9 covers the validation part. The suppression is a designed branch of the same reminder, so it is a boundary facet, not a new obligation; Codex's NOVEL label is not confirmed as a distinct clause.
status_note: Adds an explicit facet next to the original group; the original group, its ID, text and provenance are unchanged.

target_group_original.neutral_claim_text: Manifest/project-file changes not explained by a recognized command, and every removal or move, are reported with routing to add-dependency (dependency entries) or project-structure (projects/references).

distinguishing_scenario: Edit replaces a PackageReference line in a .csproj with an empty string: manifest check runs, no add-dependency reminder; the same edit adding a PackageReference produces the reminder.
facet_text: For direct edits, the reminder fires only when the edit's new text (content, new_string or edits[].new_string) contains PackageReference, PackageVersion or a "dependencies"/"devDependencies" key, or the file is package.json; removal-only edits of .csproj/Directory.Packages.props entries get no reminder.
rationale: post-tool-use.js:39-45 and 59-66 verified. FG-M1-a722465e3b says editing dependency entries 'returns a reminder'; the designed predicate inspects only the replacement/content text, so an edit that deletes a PackageReference from a .csproj (empty new_string) gets no reminder although the manifest check (FG-M1-9ab7bbe4ae) still runs. Recorded as a trigger-boundary facet; it adds no agent obligation.
status_note: Adds an explicit facet next to the original group; the original group, its ID, text and provenance are unchanged.

target_group_original.neutral_claim_text: Editing dependency entries (PackageReference/PackageVersion/dependencies or package.json) returns a reminder to confirm the add-dependency workflow was applied.

evidence.exact_excerpt:

when the client's cached representation is still valid. It carries no normal
representation and is not a generic "nothing changed" business response.
evidence.quote:
Only for a conditional request (`If-None-Match`/ETag, `If-Modified-Since`)
when the client's cached representation is still valid. It carries no normal
representation and is not a generic "nothing changed" business response.

Facet of the existing group; Codex NOVEL not confirmed as a distinct clause.

messages. Entities with identity and lifecycle remain classes unless the model
genuinely benefits from record semantics.
evidence.quote:
Good candidates: immutable transport DTOs, genuine Value Objects, immutable
messages. Entities with identity and lifecycle remain classes unless the model
genuinely benefits from record semantics.

facet_text: Exception: an entity with identity and lifecycle may use record semantics when the model genuinely benefits from them.
rationale: modern-csharp/SKILL.md:45-47 verified. FG-M1-dd5a2d04c7 (primary DEFAULT, exceptions 'none') cites lines 45-47 but omits the 'unless the model genuinely benefits' clause (protocol F6: exception inside the cited text, not stated). Under DEFAULT a justified deviation is already possible, so the explicit exception records granularity of the same rule rather than new allowed behaviour. Resolves the Codex question in favour of an explicit facet.
